top.title: Ex-Celtics Star Kyrie Irving Being Viewed as Trade Candidate Around NBA
top.description: Ex-Celtics Star Kyrie Irving Being Viewed as Trade Candidate Around NBA originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Former Boston Celtics guard Kyrie Irving has been on multiple teams throughout his career and has made an impact on many of them. Now with the Dallas Mavericks, Irving is finally back after a tough knee injury that kept him out last season. He looks like the same great player we're used to seeing, but it's not crazy to think the Mavericks could eventually move on from him, depending on how the next couple of months go. Dallas has played decent basketball this season, though it might be a bit ahead of schedule. With youngster Cooper Flagg playing as well as he has, the Mavericks might want to give him playoff experience and really go all in. We'll eventually find out if that's the plan, but if it is, there's absolutely no debate that keeping Irving on the roster at that point would make sense. However, while the Mavericks have said they want to keep Irving around for now, the latest report suggests teams across the league are expected to show interest in him, and there's still some belief he'll be dealt. “Yet when you talk to rival teams about players who would truly change the playoff landscape if they were dealt, and who are widely expected to generate serious interest because of that belief, Irving still tops the list. Never mind that the Mavericks, and Irving for that matter, have shown no signs of wanting a split. Quite the opposite, in fact,” Sam Amick wrote . Multiple teams around the NBA could use a player of Irving's caliber, including one team that could have an impact on the Celtics: the Miami Heat. Miami doesn't look like a great team right now despite landing Giannis Antetokounmpo in the offseason, which could lead them to get desperate and try to overpay for Irving. top.title: Jürgen Klopp alludes to future chances for FC Bayern’s Lennart Karl
top.description: Photo by Getty Images Jürgen Klopp’s Germany squad entered the international break needing two wins to advance to the knockout stage of the UEFA Nations League. Klopp collapsed the massive roster from his first international window into one playable unit and Germany dominated all night on the way to a 3-1 victory in Serbia. As the margins narrow, Klopp will continue to shrink the squad to maximize playing time for the best players. In the postgame interview (via @iMiaSanMia ), Klopp explained the decision making behind his squad selection process. “When you make decisions, you look at all 11 players and consider who’s covered how much ground and who you should take off,” said Klopp. “We had actually wanted to take Derry [Scherhant] off and bring Said El Mala on. But Gruda was having a bit of cramp or something like that, so I can’t just send Said back and tell him to sit down again. We were 3-1 up, and there were around 80 minutes on the clock. I know it’s not particularly nice when young players don’t start or don’t get brought on. But some players were decisive today, and tomorrow it will be others.” In the second half, Klopp opted to only utilize one of four Bayern Munich players sitting on the bench. Tom Bischof got the nod to replace his teammate, Aleksandar Pavlović. Lennart Karl, Nathaniel Brown, and Jonas Urbig watched the final whistle from the sidelines. Klopp singled out Lennart Karl as a “wonderful young man. He’s trained really, really well and is fully integrated into the team. He didn’t play today because the player who played in his position is also very good at football. But there will be many chances to come.” Join the conversation! top.title: Burnt Hills' Calhoun sets program assists record, as Spartans win 13th straight Division 2 volleyball title
top.description: Sean Calhoun of Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake serves against CBA in the Section 2 Division 2 volleyball championships at Schenectady High School in Schenectady, NY on Friday, November 13, 2026. Stephen Weaver/For the Times Union (Stephen Weaver) SCHENECTADY - Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake's starters didn't spend all that much time on the court during Friday night's Section 2 Division 2 boys' volleyball championship match against Christian Brothers Academy, but it was enough for the Spartans to stamp their authority on the match and for senior setter Sean Calhoun to make some program history. The top-seeded Spartans easily dispatched winless CBA 3-0 at Schenectady High School, winning by scores of 25-2, 25-21 and 25-17 to help the program earn its 13th consecutive sectional title. Calhoun was among the Burnt Hills (15-2 overall) players who only played during that dominant first set, but, even in his limited time on the court, the senior did enough to earn a spot in the program's record book. Among the 15 assists that Calhoun dished out during that first set was the 2,905th helper of his career, passing 2011 graduate Jordan Armstrong for the most in Burnt Hills history. Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake are the Section 2 Division 2 volleyball champions after defeating CBA at Schenectady High School in Schenectady, NY on Friday, November 13, 2026. Stephen Weaver/For the Times Union (Stephen Weaver) "It's crazy to me, thinking of all the setters who came before me - especially my brother (Aiden Calhoun). I know he's watching this right now," Calhoun said. Burnt Hills coach Paul Sander kept the approaching milestone a secret from Calhoun, who only found out when Sander called a timeout to stop the match after the senior's 2,905th assist. "We wanted it to be a real surprise for him, a real special event," Sander said. "His family knew, and the players knew, but not him. It was hard, but we kept the secret." "The only thing on my mind was states," Calhoun said. "I want states." top.title: FSU football beats Pitt, 16-10, as Seminoles defense steps up
top.description: After snapping a nearly three-year-long road losing streak with a victory over Boston College , Florida State football has now notched back-to-back wins on the road after a 16-10 win over Pitt on Friday, Nov. 13, at Acrisure Stadium. It's the first time the Seminoles have won consecutive road games since 2023, beating Wake Forest and Pitt in back-to-back weeks. With the win, FSU is one victory away from its first bowl game since 2023, and is 2-0 under interim head coach Rick Stockstill. With temperatures as low as the mid-30s in Pittsburgh, the Seminoles (5-5, 3-4 ACC) and Panthers (6-4, 3-4 ACC) played a game befitting the chilly temperatures and venue. In the home of the Steelers, FSU's defense rose to the occasion with a stout performance against a Pitt offense led by third-string true freshman quarterback Corey Dailey. He finished the night with 157 yards on 16-for-34 passing, but his interception, a pass that deflected off the back of Deamonte Diggis and into the hands of Rylan Kennedy, proved costly. FSU's lone touchdown, a one-yard rush from Amari Thomas, came off the pick. FSU's Ashton Daniels protected the football and had minimal impact on the ground (nine rushes for 27 yards) against Pitt's elite run defense. Daniels finished the night 16-of-124 for 163 yards, with the Seminoles finding primary success on screen plays. He had a fumble, which came in the red zone, but it didn't lead to any Pitt points. Here are three takeaways from the Seminoles' victory over Pitt. Seminoles offense struggles to warm up on a cold night in Pittsburgh With the exception of wide receiver Jasen Lopez, the Seminoles got little production from the offense in the first half. Lopez recorded 72 total yards on five receptions, including 58 yards in the first half on three receptions, 46 of which came on a big third-down completion. Despite Lopez setting FSU up at the 10-yard line on that 46-yard reception, it only resulted in a field goal. The Seminoles consistently struggled to find the end zone, which led to multiple field goals. Gabe Panikowski, a week after scoring a touchdown, nailed three field goals: 27 yards, 37 yards, and a 47-yarder. FSU's run game struggled in the first half against the Panthers' top-ranked rush defense, holding the team to a total of 99 yards, including 25 yards in the first half. That number was the least since FSU's clash with Clemson in 2024. The Seminoles rushed for 74 yards in the second half, including a one-yard touchdown run from Amari Thomas, the only touchdown of the game for the program. In the fourth, FSU got advantageous field position after a turnover on downs, but a red zone fumble ruined a potential momentum-swinging drive. Daniels rushed for what would have been first-down yardage on third-and-six, but after he was engulfed in a mass of both Seminoles and Panthers, he fumbled. The play wasn't blown dead for forward progress, and the ball popped out of a mass of humanity and into the grateful hands of Pitt's Shawn Lee

The Boston Red Sox have some difficult decisions to make during the Major League Baseball offseason, with Craig Breslow having to decide how he wants to improve. Breslow already made a major addition by landing Jake Bauers, who many considered one of the top free-agent bats. Reports have indicated over the past couple of days now that the Red Sox are expected to be interested in adding multiple offensive players. Per the latest report, that could even come from behind the plate. According to Jon Heyman, the Red Sox are interested in Ryan Jeffers, the 29-year-old catcher from the Minnesota Twins who finds himself in a position to get paid somewhat handsomely after posting a 127 OPS+ a year ago. "The Red Sox are a surprise pursuer of star free agent catcher Ryan Jeffers since they just traded for star catcher Adley Rutschman," Heyman wrote . This doesn't mean that the Red Sox aren't interested in keeping Adley Rutschman around, or don't think they can re-sign him when the time comes next offseason, but rather the simple fact that Boston could use another offensive guy who can swing it at a high level, and Jeffers has proven that throughout his career. top.title: 'Sandpaper scratch is totally different': Wasim Akram questions Australian bowlers' 'didn't know' defence in Sandpapergate
top.description: 'Sandpaper scratch is totally different': Wasim Akram questions Australian bowlers' 'didn't know' defence in Sandpapergate originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Wasim Akram has challenged Sandpapergate claims made by Australia Test captain Pat Cummins. His argument rests on a simple test that any fan could try. The former Pakistan pacer also offered a reminder of the values Australia has long stood for. 'Close friend' Pat Cummins put on the spot! Reverse-swing king Wasim Akram drops truth bomb on Sandpapergate Wasim Akram has a message for anyone who believes the marks left by sandpaper could pass for ordinary wear on a cricket ball. One of the finest reverse swing bowlers the sport has ever seen, the Pakistan legend has now stepped into the ball tampering row that continues to follow Australian cricket around. His message comes after Pat Cummins said on Friday that he had no idea sandpaper was being used on the ball during the infamous 2018 series in South Africa. Akram, however, finds that version of events hard to accept. One thing I was particularly looking forward to during my visit to China was seeing the famous Terracotta Warriors in Xi’an. I had read about them, seen pictures, and of course, watched films inspired by the mysteries of ancient China. But nothing quite prepared me for the experience of standing in front of thousands of life-sized soldiers who have been buried underground for more than 2,000 years. And what an experience it was! If you have watched Hollywood’s The Mummy: Tomb of the Dragon Emperor, you may remember the mysterious army of clay soldiers that comes alive. Well, I finally got to see the real thing. Thankfully, none of them came alive while I was there. But standing in those enormous exhibition halls, surrounded by thousands of soldiers, horses and chariots arranged in military formation, I couldn’t help wondering what must have gone through the minds of the people who created this extraordinary army. The story takes us back to 221 BC when Qin Shi Huang became the first emperor to unify China. Like many powerful rulers of his time, he was obsessed with immortality and the idea of continuing his reign beyond death. His solution was to build an entire underground army to protect him in the afterlife. Think about that. While some people prepared for retirement, this emperor was preparing for eternity, complete with his own military formation. The scale of the project is difficult to comprehend. Thousands of life-sized clay soldiers, horses and chariots were painstakingly created. Above the excavation pit in Xi’an, I stood where visitors have looked down on the Terracotta Army for decades: thousands of figures, each made by hand, and still not fully unearthed. What makes the discovery even more fascinating is that the soldiers are not identical. They have different facial features, hairstyles, uniforms and expressions. They look like real individuals, each with a distinct identity and military rank. Then comes another remarkable twist. nigeria.description: The Lagos University Teaching Hospital (LUTH), located at the Idi-Araba area of Lagos State, a full-fledged medical school and tertiary hospital, was established in July 1962. The federal medical institution was established to provide advanced medical services, train medical and other health care professionals and conduct research aimed at improving health care delivery in Nigeria At a point, LUTH was regarded the pride of Africa as people all over the continent came there to seek medical treatment. In 2022, the federal medical facility clocked 60. The then Chief Medical Director (CMD), Professor Chris Bode, had disclosed that the hospital had grown from a little above 300 beds to a 1000-bed medical facility and served over 25million patients. Bode said the hospital had pioneered small incision cataract excision surgery in Nigeria and trained over 40 doctors from all over the country in the procedure in the past years. He added that LUTH had also commenced laparoscopic general and gynaecologic surgery, which according to him, had dramatically reduced the duration of hospitalisation after surgery. “Since 1962, the Lagos University Teaching Hospital has contributed in no small way in the training of medical and paramedical personnel; and our products are found across all hospitals and health care facilities, both within and outside the shore of Nigeria. “As an institution, LUTH has grown from a 500-bedded hospital to 760-bed, and then to over 1000-bedded hospital serving over 25million Lagosians and its neighbouring states. “LUTH has pioneered small incision cataract excision surgery in Nigeria and has trained over 40 doctors from all over the country in the procedure in the past years. The hospital has also commenced laparoscopic general and gynaecologic surgery, which has dramatically reduced the duration of hospitalisation after surgery. “LUTH also boasts of a comprehensive diagnostic centre and VIP clinic, state of the art laboratories, radiodiagnosis, radiotherapy and renal dialysis facilities. From a humble beginning of 330 beds, LUTH today is the largest teaching hospital in Nigeria with over 1,000 beds. nigeria.title: World Diabetes Day: High cost pushes drugs, special diets out of reach
nigeria.description: As the world marks the 2026 World Diabetes Day today, attention is once again drawn to the importance of early diagnosis, timely treatment and sustained care in preventing complications and saving lives. But for many Nigerians living with the condition, the challenge goes beyond early detection to affording medication, special diets and regular medical checks needed to manage the disease. Some patients who spoke to Weekend Trust said the rising cost of treatment had pushed them into financial hardship, forcing them to ration prescribed drugs, compromise their diets or go for days without medication. For Mrs Ngunengen Akpam, living with diabetes has become a daily struggle, not only against the disease but also against the rising cost of managing it. The burden is compounded by her responsibility to also support her diabetic mother, Mama Lydia Acka, making the cost of medication, food and routine medical care a constant source of worry for the family. Akpam told one of our correspondents that the prices of essential diabetes medications had increased considerably over the years, making it increasingly difficult to maintain the treatment prescribed by her doctors. She recalled that Metformin, one of the drugs she takes, which sold for N700 for a pack of three cards in 2015, now costs about N2,500. Similarly, Dormin, which previously sold for N700, now costs N3,500 for a pack of 10 cards, she said. “The cost of drugs has increased tremendously. I take my medication twice daily, so it is not easy. In a month, we spend so much, especially when you have another diabetic person to cater for,” she said. Medication, however, is only part of the financial burden. Akpam explained that managing diabetes also requires adherence to a carefully regulated diet, including millet, beans and vegetables, which have also become expensive. Although the price of millet had dropped from more than N1,200 to N600 per mudu during the harvest season, she said her financial circumstances still made it difficult to consistently afford the recommended food items. The experience is similar for Mrs Elahi Onu, who has lived with diabetes for 11 years and whose treatment has become a major financial responsibility for her children. Onu said her children spend at least N25,000 monthly on medication alone, while more than N60,000 goes into providing the special diet recommended for managing her condition. She listed unripe plantain, beans, vegetables, basmati rice and grains such as millet among the food items she had been advised to eat. “These special types of food are costly and drain the pockets of my children. “Sometimes there is a delay in supplies of these items to me. I will be forced to go hungry for the period or fall back to any available food,” she said. Beyond feeding and medication, Onu said she also had to contend with the cost of routine medical examinations. nigeria.description: On Saturday, November 7, Nigeria’s Flamingos edged out Asian giants Japan 2-1 in Rabat, Morocco, to lift the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. They became the first African nation to claim the global title and placed Nigeria alongside France as the only countries to win both the men’s and women’s U-17 World Cups. The Flamingos’ male counterparts, the Golden Eaglets—with five titles—remain the most successful team in the world at that level. The victorious Flamingos returned to Nigeria on Monday, November 9, to a rousing welcome. Yet amid the national celebrations, federal cash rewards, and Senate commendations, a familiar anxiety lingers over the future of the young players. For decades, Nigeria has dominated youth tournaments, only to watch many of its brightest teenage sensations fade into obscurity. While stars like Victor Osimhen and Asisat Oshoala successfully transitioned to the global stage, countless others, hampered by poor management, unhealed injuries, or structural neglect, abandoned football altogether before their prime. Indeed, the history of Nigerian football is replete with stories of teenage sensations who sparkled at dawn with youth national teams only to fade into obscurity before noon. Thus, in spite of Nigeria’s dominance at the U-17 level, the country is yet to taste global victory at the U-20 level. The Flying Eagles, the team meant to harness the best talent from victorious U-17 squads, have managed to claim only two silver medals and one bronze since their first appearance in 1983. Similarly, only a handful of players have successfully transitioned from the U-17 to the U-20 and senior Super Eagles squads. Nduka Ugbade, Jonathan Akpoborie, Celestine Babayaro, Mikel Obi, Chinedu Obasi, Lukman Haruna, Ramon Azeez, Isaac Success and Taiwo Awoniyi are among the few who completed the full international pathway. Nigerias’ Flamingos U17 celebrating their World Cup win To ensure the 2026 Flamingos squad, and the next generation of young Nigerian athletes, don’t become cautionary tales, Nigerian football administrators must shift their focus from one-off tournament celebrations to sustainable career architecture. One of the biggest leaks in Nigerian football happens immediately after a youth tournament ends. Without a centralised database, young players return to disorganised local setups and vanish from national team radars. It is, therefore, a step in the right direction that the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) has promised to preserve the core of the victorious Flamingos, with 11 players still eligible for the next U-17 competition. Meanwhile, the federation stated that others would be groomed for the U-20 national team, the Falconets, and eventually the Super Falcons. nigeria.title: Emefiele: Court admits Supreme Court judgment in forfeiture case
nigeria.description: —Restricts use of document in ongoing criminal trial By Henry Ojelu The Lagos State Special Offences Court, Ikeja, on Friday admitted a Supreme Court judgment tendered by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission, EFCC, in the ongoing trial of former Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, Godwin Emefiele, over the forfeiture of properties allegedly linked to him. However, the trial judge, Justice Rahman Oshodi, ruled that although the judgment was admissible, it could not be used for or against any of the parties in the criminal proceedings. Ruling on objections raised by the defence, led by Olalekan Ojo, SAN, and submissions by the prosecution, led by the Federal Director of Public Prosecutions, Rotimi Oyedepo, SAN, Justice Oshodi held that the document was a public document and a certified true copy of a Supreme Court decision. The judge consequently admitted it as Exhibit A but restricted its use in the trial. He said: “The judgment is a public document, and it is a certified true copy of the Supreme Court decision. It would be accepted as an exhibit (in rem), but cannot be used in the case either for or against any party.” Justice Oshodi explained that the document satisfied the legal requirements for admissibility under the Evidence Act. On the defence’s objection that the prosecution tendered only the lead judgment without the separate judgments of other Supreme Court justices, the judge relied on the Court of Appeal decision in Matthias Sikiri and Others v. Nketchukwu Onyema and Others (2021) LPELR-56552(CA). He also cited Avacha and Others v. Fawole, where the Supreme Court held that the lead judgment represents the decision of the court. Addressing concerns over the use of a judgment arising from civil forfeiture proceedings in a criminal trial, Justice Oshodi said the restriction on its use had adequately addressed the issue. Citing David Itauma v. Friday Jasi, the judge said previous judgments tendered in subsequent proceedings were intended to establish what was decided in the earlier cases and not to prove the guilt or innocence of parties in the subsequent proceedings. He consequently overruled the defence objection and admitted the document. Earlier, Ojo had opposed its admission, arguing that the judgment was irrelevant to the charges against his client, incomplete without the other justices’ opinions and arose from non-conviction-based civil forfeiture proceedings. Counsel to the second defendant, A.M. Kotoye, SAN, aligned himself with the objection and urged the court to reject the document. However, Oyedepo argued that the judgment was admissible as a certified true copy of a Supreme Court decision, adding that the prosecution had complied with Sections 103 and 104 of the Evidence Act. He maintained that the fact that only the lead judgment was tendered did not affect its admissibility, while the civil nature of the forfeiture proceedings did not make the document inadmissible. Real Madrid’s Silva, who inherits the captain’s armband from Ronaldo, admitted that the striker had been the main focus for much of the past two decades but backed the team to cope with the pressure in the 41-year-old’s absence. “Everyone knows the weight Cristiano carries. Most people went to the stadium to see Cristiano, many went just for him, and that’s not going to happen now,” Silva told reporters. “The national team players are used to the spotlight, the pressure, and the responsibility, as well as being pointed at when things don’t go well — so that’s not an issue.” Portugal will pay tribute to five-time Ballon d’Or winner Ronaldo before the game against Denmark, with media reporting the squad will walk out wearing number seven jerseys, Ronaldo’s number. Whether Ronaldo will be present is unknown, after he fell out with veteran coach Jorge Jesus in September. Last week Ronaldo said he was bringing down the curtain on his storied international career. nigeria.title: FG records 16 Nigerian deaths in Addis Ababa, warns travellers
nigeria.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja The Federal Government has warned Nigerians, particularly those with pre-existing medical conditions, to exercise caution when travelling through Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, following the deaths of 16 Nigerians in the city this year. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs disclosed this in a travel advisory issued on Friday, stating that the deaths recorded by Nigeria’s Diplomatic Mission in Addis Ababa were reportedly linked to health complications associated with the city’s high altitude. The ministry explained that Addis Ababa is situated approximately 2,355 metres (7,726 feet) above sea level, where lower atmospheric pressure results in reduced oxygen availability. It noted that the conditions could pose increased health risks to travellers with certain underlying medical conditions, particularly cardiovascular and respiratory ailments. According to the advisory, although healthy individuals are generally able to adapt to reduced oxygen levels in high-altitude environments, people with certain pre-existing health conditions may experience complications. The Federal Government therefore advised Nigerians whose medical conditions could be worsened by high altitudes to seek appropriate medical advice before undertaking journeys involving transit through the Ethiopian capital. It also urged travellers with underlying medical conditions to consult medical professionals and obtain necessary guidance before embarking on their trips. The ministry, however, clarified that the advisory was not intended to discourage Nigerians from travelling to or transiting through Addis Ababa. Rather, it said the notice was aimed at ensuring that medically vulnerable travellers were adequately informed about the possible effects of high altitudes and took necessary precautions. The advisory stated, “This year, Nigeria’s Diplomatic Mission in Addis Ababa has recorded 16 deaths involving Nigerians transiting through the city, reportedly linked to health complications associated with high altitudes. “While healthy individuals are generally able to adapt to reduced oxygen levels in high-altitude environments, persons with certain pre-existing medical ailments, particularly cardiovascular and respiratory conditions, may experience increased health risks in such conditions. “In view of the foregoing, Nigerians with pre-existing health conditions that can be exacerbated by high altitudes are strongly advised to exercise caution when planning journeys that involve transit through Addis Ababa. “Travellers with underlying medical conditions are also urged to obtain appropriate medical guidance before undertaking such journeys.” The ministry reiterated that the advisory was not intended to discourage Nigerians from travelling to or transiting through Addis Ababa but to ensure that those vulnerable to the physiological effects of high altitudes were adequately informed. nigeria.title: Goalkeeper Owono suspended for 12 matches after De Miguel death
nigeria.description: FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono was suspended for 12 matches by the Spanish football federation’s disciplinary committee on Friday after his challenge on Jesus de Miguel resulted in the death of the Tenerife striker last week. Equatorial Guinea international Owono was sent off in the second division clash on November 2 after racing into midfield and colliding with De Miguel while trying to clear an aerial ball. After the collision De Miguel, 30, was placed in intensive care in hospital and the Spanish forward died on November 3. “The assessment of the conduct under consideration in these proceedings must be based on the facts expressly recorded in the referee’s report, which states that the player was sent off for ‘violently striking an opponent in the chest with his leg, using excessive force, while the ball was in play’,” said the committee in a statement. “The tragic outcome of the incident, resulting in the death of Jesus de Miguel Alameda, is public knowledge. “In view of the nature of the conduct described and the accompanying circumstances… the maximum sanction, 12 matches of suspension, is justified.” Spanish police sources last week told AFP an investigation into what happened had been opened under judicial supervision. Owono said he was enduring the “hardest days of my life” after De Miguel’s death. “These are the hardest days of my life. I struggle to find the words and it is very difficult for me to process anything that has happened,” said Owono in a statement published by his club Andorra last week. “I feel immense pain over the loss of Jesus. I think of him, of his family, and of all the people who loved him. “I know there will be many issues to address, and I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect. But right now, honestly, I cannot think about anything other than Jesus and the pain we are going through. Rest in peace, Jesus.” FC Andorra coach Carles Manso said Thursday it would be Owono who decides if and when he returns to football after the tragic incident. On Saturday Tenerife fans and players gathered at the club’s stadium for a memorial and farewell to De Miguel. His funeral took place last Thursday and around 400 mourners attended, including Spain coach Luis de la Fuente and Real Madrid president Florentino Perez. nigeria.title: Tinubu Hails Bakassi Seaport, Says Project Will Create Jobs, Boost Trade
nigeria.description: President Bola Tinubu has described the groundbreaking of the Bakassi Deep Seaport in Cross River State as a major milestone in Nigeria’s economic diversification, saying the project will open new commercial corridors, stimulate industrialisation and create jobs. The President recalled that the project was conceived in 2014, with an Environmental and Social Impact Assessment developed in March 2015, before receiving fresh impetus under Otu. Designed with a 20-metre draft, the port is expected to accommodate large vessels that currently bypass Nigerian ports. It is also linked to a 260-kilometre superhighway intended to facilitate the movement of cargo to markets across the country. Tinubu credited Otu’s determination with helping to overcome institutional and financial challenges, including efforts to secure a $3.5 billion financing arrangement with Afreximbank and formalise the Public-Private Partnership framework in February 2025. “This is beyond a Cross River dream. He argued that establishing another major maritime gateway would reduce pressure on Lagos ports, ease congestion and lower costs. “When Calabar works, Nigeria works on two legs,” the President added. He said Nigeria had not fully exploited its coastline along the Gulf of Guinea, while neighbouring countries continued to benefit from trade that could be attracted to Nigerian ports. Tinubu said the Bakassi project would help retain regional cargo, expand access to international markets and strengthen Nigeria’s competitiveness in maritime trade. He noted that about 90 per cent of cargo moves by sea, but Nigeria handles only a fraction of regional cargo trade despite its economic position in West Africa. nigeria.title: Lagos NDC meeting attack threatens democracy — APM candidate
nigeria.description: By Dapo Akinrefon The governorship candidate of the Action Peoples Movement (APM) in Lagos State, Prince Laja Adeoye, has condemned the attack on supporters of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) during their town hall meeting in Lagos, describing the incident as shameful and a threat to democracy. Adeoye said the disruption of the meeting at Classique Event Centre, Oregun, Ikeja, on Thursday, amounted to an infringement on the constitutional rights of citizens to assemble and freely express their political views. He warned that the use of thugs to disrupt opposition gatherings could heighten political tension ahead of the 2027 general elections. Adeoye said, “Nobody should be attacked for supporting a candidate of his or her choice. What happened in Lagos on Thursday was shameful and unacceptable in a democracy.” He described the incident as particularly disturbing, noting that Lagos had traditionally been regarded as a centre of political activities where parties and candidates could canvass for support. According to him, the attack was not merely against the NDC but also against the democratic process and Nigerians who believe in free and fair elections. The APM candidate urged the Lagos State Police Command to identify, arrest and prosecute those responsible for the incident, irrespective of their political affiliation or status. He warned that failure to bring the perpetrators to justice could encourage similar attacks in other parts of the country as political activities gather momentum ahead of the 2027 elections. Adeoye also expressed concern over the safety of voters, candidates and journalists during the campaign period, recalling reports that a journalist covering the meeting was attacked and dispossessed of his working equipment. He called on political leaders to rise above partisan interests and condemn violence, stressing that democracy could not thrive in an atmosphere of fear and intimidation. The APM candidate commended the NDC supporters for maintaining their composure despite the alleged provocation, saying their conduct demonstrated commitment to democratic values. “The supporters did not retaliate. They conducted themselves in a peaceful manner. That is the spirit we need to sustain our democracy,” he said. Adeoye also called on the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), security agencies and other political stakeholders to work together to guarantee a level playing field for all parties ahead of the 2027 elections. nigeria.title: Nasarawa pensioners begin enforcement of ₦4bn court order
nigeria.description: By Edwin Philip, Lafia A group of 601 retired civil servants in Nasarawa State has commenced enforcement of a court order directing the recovery of over ₦4 billion in outstanding gratuities and other entitlements owed them by the state government. The pensioners, under the aegis of the Concerned Group of Nasarawa State Pensioners, secured a consent judgment against the state government in 2020 over the alleged non-payment of their retirement benefits. Their spokespersons, Mr Simon Auna and Mallam Usman Adamu, disclosed the development while speaking with journalists in Lafia on Friday. The group said it subsequently obtained an order from the National Industrial Court, Makurdi, awarding 25 per cent post-judgment interest on the judgment sum, bringing the total amount being sought to over ₦4 billion. According to the pensioners, following the alleged failure of the state government to comply with the judgment, their lawyers approached the Senior District Court in Makurdi, presided over by Justice Ada Jack. The court subsequently directed six commercial banks to release funds belonging to the Nasarawa State Government, amounting to over ₦4 billion, for payment to the affected retirees. In a move to enforce the order, the pensioners’ legal team, accompanied by court bailiffs, visited some branches of one of the commercial banks in Makurdi, Benue State, where they removed some movable properties. Speaking on the development, counsel to the pensioners, Mrs Doofan Sefa-Aii, said the legal team would continue to operate within the law to ensure full recovery of the funds owed the retirees. Another counsel, Mr Awo Matthew, appealed to the Nasarawa State Government and the banks involved to allow the legal process to take its course, considering the hardship the pensioners had endured while pursuing payment of their entitlements. However, the Director of Corporate Services and Arbitration at the Nasarawa State Ministry of Justice, Mr Usman Aliyu, said the state government had taken all necessary legal steps, including filing a motion for a stay of execution of the court order. Meanwhile, Adamu, who is the group’s Lafia Local Government Chairman, and Auna, its Legal Adviser, described the court order as a significant breakthrough after years of seeking payment of their entitlements. They said the development had renewed their hope of recovering the outstanding benefits. The pensioners reaffirmed their determination to pursue their entitlements through lawful means until the matter was resolved. nigeria.title: Zulum offers soldiers N50,000 each, logistics for Borno deployment
nigeria.description: By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri Borno State Governor, Professor Babagana Umara Zulum, has announced a ₦50,000 welfare support for each soldier preparing for deployment to Maiwa and Koshebe communities in the state, alongside a pledge to provide operational logistics to strengthen security. Zulum gave the assurance on Friday during a visit to the headquarters of the 24 Task Force Brigade in Dikwa Local Government Area, where he met with the Brigade Commander, Brigadier General Aminu Gumel. The governor said the visit was aimed at exploring measures to improve security along the Maiduguri–Mafa–Dikwa–Ngala highway, a strategic economic corridor linking several communities in eastern Borno State. He noted that the highway was vital to trade, transportation and cross-border commercial activities, stressing that improved security would enable residents to travel safely, move agricultural produce and rebuild their livelihoods. “My visit is primarily aimed at exploring measures to strengthen security along the strategic economic corridor, which connects Maiduguri to several communities in eastern Borno and serves as a vital route for trade, transportation and cross-border commercial activities,” Zulum said. Addressing troops preparing for deployment to Maiwa and Koshebe, the governor pledged to provide operational logistics and sustained welfare support. He also announced a payment of ₦50,000 to each soldier preparing for the deployment to the two communities. Koshebe has previously suffered deadly attacks by suspected Boko Haram insurgents. On November 28, 2020, insurgents attacked rice farmers working in fields around the community, killing more than 100 people, many of whom were seasonal farm labourers from Sokoto State. Similarly, in November 2023, suspected insurgents attacked farmers harvesting rice in the Karkut and Koshebe areas of Mafa Local Government Area, killing at least 13 people, while others were reported missing. Zulum’s administration has continued to provide logistics and welfare assistance to security agencies as part of efforts to support military operations, improve security and facilitate the return of displaced residents to their communities. The governor was accompanied on the visit by the member representing Monguno/Nganzai/Marte Federal Constituency in the House of Representatives, Engr. Bukar Talba; member representing Dikwa Constituency in the Borno State House of Assembly, Mohammed Zakariya; Commissioner for Information and Internal Security, Professor Usman Tar; Commissioner for Local Government and Emirate Affairs, Sugun Mai Mele; and other senior government officials. nigeria.title: COVID-19 loans must be repaid, NIRSAL MFB insists
nigeria.description: By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief NIRSAL Microfinance Bank (NMFB) has clarified that the COVID-19 Targeted Credit Facility (TCF) was an intervention loan, not a grant, stressing that beneficiaries are obligated to repay the funds. The bank said deductions from the accounts of beneficiaries who accessed the facility would continue until their outstanding loans were fully liquidated, in line with the Global Standing Instruction (GSI) mechanism. In a statement issued in Abuja at the weekend, the bank explained that the GSI framework allows financial institutions to recover outstanding loan obligations from eligible accounts linked to borrowers’ Bank Verification Numbers (BVNs), subject to applicable regulatory guidelines. The bank said the clarification became necessary to address concerns surrounding loan recoveries and reassure customers and members of the public of its commitment to transparency, accountability and responsible banking practices. It explained that the COVID-19 Targeted Credit Facility was introduced by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) to support households and businesses affected by the economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. According to the bank, all beneficiaries were required to accept electronic offer letters before disbursement, with the documents clearly outlining the terms and conditions of the facility, including repayment obligations and recovery mechanisms in cases of default. “Regarding the recovery process, the Bank operates within the applicable regulatory framework, including the Global Standing Instruction (GSI) mechanism approved by the Central Bank of Nigeria,” it stated. NIRSAL MFB, however, acknowledged concerns raised by some beneficiaries over the timing and amounts of deductions, outstanding loan balances and access to repayment information. The bank said it took the complaints seriously, noting that customers must have access to accurate information about their loan accounts. It stressed that the deductions were intended to settle outstanding contractual obligations, adding that beneficiaries who disputed deductions or identified discrepancies in their repayment records should contact the bank for individual account reconciliation. “Where any beneficiary has concerns about deductions made, discrepancies in repayment records or the status of an outstanding balance, such cases should be brought to the bank’s attention for individual account reconciliation and appropriate resolution,” it said. The bank assured that legitimate complaints would be investigated and that any discrepancies established during the reconciliation process would receive the necessary attention. It urged beneficiaries seeking clarification on their loan status, repayment history or outstanding obligations to contact the bank through its officially designated customer service channels. nigeria.title: Customs intercepts live sea turtle at Nigeria-Benin border
nigeria.description: By Efe Onodjae The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS), Seme Area Command, has intercepted a live endangered sea turtle allegedly being smuggled through a footpath linking Nigeria and the Republic of Benin. The Olive Ridley Sea Turtle, scientifically known as Lepidochelys olivacea, was intercepted during a routine patrol by Customs officers at about 10.30pm on Thursday, November 12, 2026. The command said the officers sighted a suspicious individual carrying a sack along the border route, but the suspect abandoned the bag and fled into a nearby bush upon noticing the patrol team. According to a statement by the command’s Public Relations Officer, Superintendent of Customs, John Tunde Ayagbalo, examination of the abandoned sack revealed the live sea turtle concealed inside. He said the animal was immediately secured and kept in safe custody before being handed over to relevant wildlife authorities for proper care, rehabilitation and eventual release into its natural habitat. The Acting Customs Area Controller, Seme Area Command, Deputy Comptroller Norman Olisah Alumanah, described the interception as a demonstration of the vigilance and professionalism of officers in tackling wildlife trafficking. Alumanah warned smugglers, poachers and their collaborators against using the nation’s borders as corridors for illegal wildlife trade, adding that the command had intensified patrols, surveillance and intelligence gathering across its area of responsibility. He also called on residents of border communities to provide credible intelligence to support the fight against wildlife trafficking. The Customs boss said the command would complement enforcement operations with stakeholder education and sensitisation on endangered species, their ecological importance and the legal implications of their unauthorised trade. Wildlife trafficking remains a major environmental crime, threatening biodiversity and the survival of endangered species through illegal exploitation for meat, eggs, shells, traditional medicine and the exotic pet trade. Nigeria is a signatory to the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES), which regulates international trade in endangered wildlife and plant species. The convention is domesticated in Nigeria through the Endangered Species (Control of International Trade and Traffic) Act, Cap E9, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria, 2004. nigeria.title: Ebola: All 62 contacts test negative after monitoring – NCDC
nigeria.description: By Chidinma Chukwu ABUJA — The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) has completed the 21-day monitoring of all 62 contacts linked to the imported case of Bundibugyo Virus Disease (BVD), a form of Ebola disease, confirmed in the Federal Capital Territory on October 20, 2026, with no secondary infections recorded. The Director-General of NCDC, Dr Jide Idris, disclosed this on Friday during a media briefing in Abuja, saying the last contact had been discharged from monitoring after testing negative for the virus. Idris said 13 of the 62 contacts reported fever or other non-specific symptoms during the monitoring period, but laboratory tests confirmed that none had contracted the disease. “The 21-day monitoring period for contacts linked to the index case has been completed, with the last contact discharged today. We are glad to announce that none of the contacts became ill with the disease, meaning no transmission from the index case. “A total of 62 contacts were identified, placed in quarantine and followed up by our public health teams. During the monitoring period, 13 contacts reported fever or other non-specific symptoms. All 13 were tested for Bundibugyo Virus Disease, and all tested negative,” he said. The index case was a 42-year-old Ugandan-born woman, who tested positive for the virus in Abuja on October 20. She was subsequently medically evacuated to Switzerland on October 26. Providing an update on her condition, Idris said the woman had recovered and been discharged from a hospital in Geneva. He also disclosed that seven additional suspected cases were reported and investigated in Adamawa, Rivers, Borno, Lagos and Ekiti states within the past three weeks. All seven cases tested negative for the virus. However, the NCDC chief cautioned against interpreting the completion of contact monitoring as a formal declaration that the outbreak was over. He explained that such a declaration would depend on established public health criteria and findings from continued surveillance. “It is important to note that the completion of contact monitoring does not, by itself, constitute a formal declaration that an outbreak is over. Such a determination must be based on the applicable public health criteria and the findings of ongoing surveillance. “Nigeria therefore remains vigilant, particularly given the continued occurrence of Ebola virus disease in the DRC,” he said. Idris assured Nigerians that disease surveillance and preparedness activities would continue, stressing that the agency remained committed to protecting residents and visitors. Looking ahead to the December festive season, he warned that increased travel, social interactions and large public gatherings could heighten the risk of disease transmission. nigeria.title: 2027: Tinubu, Atiku, Obi not there for Nigeria — Sule Lamido
nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Former Jigawa State Governor and PDP chieftain, Sule Lamido, has dismissed President Bola Tinubu, former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar and former Anambra State Governor, Peter Obi, as unsuitable options for Nigeria ahead of the 2027 general election. Lamido stated this during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Friday, where he was asked which of the three political figures could attract the Northern vote in the forthcoming presidential election. Giving his assessment, the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) chieftain said none of the three contenders was in a position to address Nigeria’s challenges. He said, “Look, from my own personal opinion, in my view, voting should depend on who is the person with the right kind of quality and calibre to be able to address the same problem. Peter Obi, Tinubu, Atiku — none of them is there for Nigeria.” The former Jigawa governor also declared his support for the PDP’s presidential candidate, Professor Sandy Onor, insisting that he remained committed to the opposition party and would not vote for Tinubu in 2027. Asked whether he had endorsed Tinubu for a second term, Lamido said he remained a PDP member and would vote for his party’s candidate. He said, “I am PDP through and through. I am voting for my candidate, Professor Sandy Onor; that is my candidate. What I’m saying is that we have somebody called Professor Onor on that ballot. I’m voting him.” Lamido’s remarks come amid controversy over claims that he had endorsed Tinubu’s re-election bid after Vice-President Kashim Shettima reportedly listed him among former Jigawa governors backing the President ahead of 2027. However, the Jigawa State chapter of the PDP had earlier dismissed the claim, insisting that Lamido had neither endorsed Tinubu nor defected to the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC. entertainment.title: FWIFT 2026 Convention Communique: Industry Leaders Charge Women in Media to Embrace Cross-Border Growth
entertainment.description: The Forum for Women in Film and Television Nigeria (FWIFT) successfully concluded its 2026 annual convention on Thursday, October 29, at the historic Glover Memorial Hall in Lagos, Nigeria. Convening under the theme “One Industry, Many Voices: Building Together,” the afternoon brought together over 200 practitioners from several sectors including; film, television, radio, advertising, and digital media to connect, share insights, and build mutual agency. Supported by the African Women’s Development Fund (AWDF) , the convention featured a keynote address by cultural curator Sandra Mbanefo Obiago , interactive panel sessions, break-out workshops, speed networking, and a flagship fireside chat titled “The Cross Over: A Career Beyond Borders.” The event drew leading voices from across the creative economy, including media executive Kadaria Ahmed , filmmaker Biodun Stephens, media personality Gbemi Olateru-Olagbegi, executive director Rosemary Egabor-Afolahan, and director Esosa Osagiede. Key takeaways and actionable resolutions from the convention sessions emphasized resilience, strategic partnerships, and structural evolution: Embrace Bold Collaboration and Risk-Taking: Speakers urged media professionals to shed apprehension around institutional partnerships. As highlighted during the panel discussions: “Do not allow fear of failing stop you from asking for help, do your due diligence on the people you want to partner with then go for it. If it does not work, do not stop, get up and go again.” Adaptability as a Survival Imperative: In an era of rapid technological and digital shifts across broadcast and film, participants were reminded of the absolute necessity of evolution: “If you don’t change with the times, you will grow stale.” Deconstructing Industry Myths: Addressing professional dynamics, panelists challenged antiquated narratives regarding female competition, affirming that systemic progress relies on solidarity: “Women work well with women, it is a myth that they do not.” FWIFT’s leadership noted that the conversations at Glover Memorial Hall mark a critical step toward cementing cross-sector alliances. The forum remains committed to translating these insights into actionable frameworks, mentorship programs, and policy advocacy for women shaping the future of African media. For more information on upcoming FWIFT initiatives, programs, and future events, visit the official website or follow @fwiftnigeria on social media. There is a lot that goes into establishing a successful business. It requires developing the business idea, securing clients, building a customer base and eventually bringing people on board. I once worked with a client who needed a new set of employees for a business establishment that was reopening after a period of restructuring. The manager would oversee the day-to-day running of the establishment, ensure that company policies were implemented and periodically train employees based on the requirements of their respective roles. The challenge was that the new management structure had not been properly implemented within the organisation. Unfortunately, when she called, I couldn’t talk on the phone as I had been ambushed by my kids, who were brandishing their homework and threatening to cry if I didn’t help them. As a mom herself, she immediately understood why I couldn’t continue with the conversation. I quickly made my excuses, and we laughed and hung up, promising to catch up at a more convenient time. However, that exchange got me thinking about how most millennial women have a radically different marriage and motherhood timeline from our mothers. You see, when my mother was in her early 40s, my siblings and I were in university, so she had a lot of free time during the week to spend relaxing, hanging out with her friends, and attending social events. Basically living her best life. I, on the other hand, at 40-plus, spend my days cooking pot after pot of hot meals that immediately get devoured by my ever-hungry kids, teaching my nursery school-aged kids how to count and spell, and trying but often failing to enforce a strict bedtime with yelling and threats. I constantly feel myself going underwater and have to fight for my life every single day. There are other ways motherhood has been such a hugely different experience for me than it was for my mother. Like many women of her generation, she got married right after secondary school as university education was not seen as vital. This meant that she was a teenage mother and so had more energy to spare on her kids. She also benefited from having a lot of support from domestic staff and relatives. I do not have any village supporting me with child-rearing. I have hired domestic staff in the past, but it was always one thing or another, and they ended up leaving me stranded. I also do not have youth on my side, and I have the back pain and other aches to prove it. But this experience is not unique to me. Statistics show that most women globally will have their first child at 30 or 31, and we are seeing a lot more women becoming first-time moms at 35 and above. This is considered advanced maternal age. The fact is that as women increasingly prioritise university education and career stability before marriage, maternal age will continue to rise. This is not a trend that can be reversed. The wobbly Nigerian economy doesn’t help matters either, as people are putting off marriage till they can grow their finances, leading to advanced marital age across both genders. For instance, I have several male ex-classmates in their 40s who have given up on getting married because they cannot afford to. This is very unfortunate. entertainment.title: Toni Tones and Jim Iyke Are Bringing Drama to KAVA This November — See the Official Poster
entertainment.description: The Nigerian thriller series, directed by Wande Thomas and produced by Isoken Ogiemwonyi, is set to join KAVA’s growing slate of premium African content. Nigerian streaming platform KAVA is set to bring the psychological thriller series Spiraling , starring Toni Tones ( King of Boys ) and Jim Iyke , to audiences across its streaming service. Set against the high-stakes worlds of technology, power and politics in contemporary Nigeria, Spiraling follows Sade ( Toni Tones ), a brilliant tech entrepreneur whose carefully constructed life begins to unravel after an impulsive affair triggers a dangerous chain of events. Spiraling explores the darker side of ambition and the lengths people will go to protect their carefully constructed lives. Alongside Tones and Iyke, the ensemble cast includes Folu Storms , Seun Ajayi , Fae Olumide , Fiyinfoluwa Asenuga and Mathilda Akatugba . Created and directed by Wande Thomas ( Under the Influence , The Smart Money Woman ), the series is co-written by Thomas and Amaka Anioji and produced by Isoken Ogiemwonyi ( The Smart Money Woman , Ci ) . Director and creator Wande Thomas added: I wanted to explore how quickly an ordinary decision can spiral into something completely beyond your control. At its heart, this is a story about the secrets we keep, the lies we tell ourselves and how far we’ll go when everything is at stake. I’m excited for audiences to finally experience it. F Taofeeq/Spiraling Producer Isoken Ogiemwonyi said: With Spiraling , we wanted to take a simple story and tell it really well. We spent a lot of time developing the characters and exploring the darker side of very human emotions, ambition, desire and jealousy. At its heart, it’s a character-driven story about flawed people making questionable decisions, and we’re excited to partner with KAVA to bring it to audiences across Africa and the diaspora. Ladun Awobokun , Head of Acquisitions at KAVA commented : Spiraling is exactly the kind of bold, sophisticated African storytelling we want to champion at KAVA. With its compelling performances and distinctly Nigerian setting, the series delivers a gripping thriller that we believe will resonate with audiences at home and around the world. We’re delighted to bring it to our viewers. Spiraling will be available to stream on KAVA on the 26th of November. Follow @spiralingseries for updates. entertainment.title: “Lagos Gave Me My Greatest Successes and Deepest Heartbreak”: DJ Cuppy Opens Up in Ifeoluwa Documentary
entertainment.description: Nigerian DJ and philanthropist Florence Otedola, popularly known as Cuppy, pictured wearing gold headphones and a camel-brown blazer. On her birthday, Florence Ifeoluwa Otedola is giving viewers a more personal glimpse into her life, exploring home, family, identity and purpose. For years, Nigerians have known Florence “Cuppy” Otedola as the internationally recognised DJ and philanthropist, often recognised by her signature pink hair and vibrant public personality. This birthday, however, her new documentary offers a closer look at the woman behind that familiar public image. Released on 11 November 2026, her new 12-minute documentary, Ifeoluwa , follows Cuppy back to Lagos, the city that shaped her and remains close to her heart. It is also a place connected to some of her greatest successes and deepest heartbreak. The title Ifeoluwa means “The Love of God”. Rather than marking the occasion with another glamorous birthday celebration, Cuppy has chosen to share a more reflective portrait of her life. The film explores womanhood, ambition, identity, belonging and the ongoing process of becoming. There are tender moments, too. Viewers see Cuppy not just as a public figure, but as a daughter, sister and granddaughter. Her time with her grandmother offers an especially intimate glimpse into the affection and family ties at the heart of her story. The documentary also captures an evolution audiences may already have noticed. Her signature pink hair has given way to a new look, while faith, education and service have become increasingly central to how Cuppy speaks about her future. This is not a rejection of music, but a fuller picture of the person behind it. Her philanthropic work remains an important part of that picture. Through the Cuppy Foundation, she has helped raise more than $17 million to support displaced children in Nigeria, in partnership with Save the Children. She has also established education funds at the University of Oxford, New York University and King’s College London to help students overcome financial barriers, particularly those from Africa. Alongside this work, Cuppy remains active as an international DJ, with performances at Glastonbury, Wireless Festival and Cannes Lions, as well as events during United Nations General Assembly week. At its heart, Ifeoluwa is a personal homecoming that brings together family, faith, Lagos and the experiences shaping Cuppy’s next chapter. It offers viewers a chance to see beyond the familiar celebrity image and learn more about the person behind it. entertainment.title: Olamide’s Time & Space Is Almost Here! See the Cover Art & 10 Track List
entertainment.description: Olamide releases his new single Burukutu alongside his upcoming album Time & Space. Photo Credit: Olamide/Instagram If Olamide ‘s ‘ Burukutu ‘ has been on repeat, here’s something else to get into: the rapper has revealed the cover art and full tracklist for his upcoming album, Time & Space . Scheduled for release on November 16, 2026, under YBNL Nation and EMPIRE, the ten-track body of work follows a remarkable lineage of musical evolution from one of Africa’s most enduring creative forces. Adding a deeply personal touch to the rollout, Olamide revealed that he personally painted the striking cover art for the project. Olamide hand-painted the official artwork for his upcoming Time & Space, released via YBNL Nation and EMPIRE. Photo Credit: Olamide/Instagram Listeners have already caught an exciting glimpse of what to expect from the record through the release of the lead single, Burukutu . Named after the traditional, locally brewed fermented grain beverage, the track serves up rich street-level jubilation and celebratory culture, anchored by rhythmic cadences and unmistakable Yoruba-inflected delivery. The musical journey of Time & Space spans ten carefully curated titles designed to showcase his artistic range. The newly revealed tracklist opens with “ Elohim ” as the introductory piece, followed sequentially by “ Skoskola “, “ Say Less “, the lead anthem “ Burukutu “, and “ Alujon ” rounding out the first half. As November 16 approaches, anticipation continues to build across Lagos and beyond, cementing yet another brilliant chapter in Olamide’s legendary catalogue. entertainment.description: Alex Unusual’s gold grillz, crystal floral choker, and cherub-accented sunglasses. Who says a buba has to be paired with a wrapper? Nigerian actress, media personality, and reality television star Asogwa Alexandra A —popularly known as Alex Unusua l—is giving us another way to wear the traditional Yoruba top, and her look for the premiere of Loving Itohan makes a strong case for pairing it with a mini skirt. The actress chose a bright fuchsia satin buba with wide half-sleeves, styling it with a fitted mini skirt made from emerald-green and magenta floral brocade damask . It’s an interesting way to rethink the familiar iro and bubacombination: keep the traditional top, swap the wrapper for a shorter skirt, and let the difference in fabric and colour give the outfit its character. The smooth finish of the pink satin against the patterned damask also shows how to wear two statement fabrics without making them compete . The trick is to give each piece a clear role, with the pink buba providing a bold block of colour and the brocade bringing in pattern and texture. Alex Unusual puts a modern spin on the Yoruba iro and buba with a satin top and brocade mini skirt. The mini skirt also gives the outfit a contemporary take on the Oleku silhouette, which traditionally pairs a loose or fitted buba with a wrapper tied above the knee. Alex’s version plays with that familiar proportion, using a fitted damask skirt in place of the wrapper. If you are wondering how to wear a buba and mini skirt without the proportions feeling off, the secret is balancing volume with structure. Because a traditional buba comes with a relaxed cut and wide sleeves, tucking it cleanly into a fitted, high-waisted mini skirt defines the waist and keeps the silhouette neat rather than boxy. Mixing textures intentionally helps too—pairing a plain silk, satin, or AsoOke top with a patterned damask, jacquard, or beaded mini skirt lets both pieces complement each other rather than clash. Using the same fabric for the skirt and gele also helped bring the different parts of the outfit together, while keeping the pink buba at the centre of the colour story. sports.title: FSU football beats Pitt, 16-10, as Seminoles defense steps up
sports.description: After snapping a nearly three-year-long road losing streak with a victory over Boston College , Florida State football has now notched back-to-back wins on the road after a 16-10 win over Pitt on Friday, Nov. 13, at Acrisure Stadium. It's the first time the Seminoles have won consecutive road games since 2023, beating Wake Forest and Pitt in back-to-back weeks. With the win, FSU is one victory away from its first bowl game since 2023, and is 2-0 under interim head coach Rick Stockstill. With temperatures as low as the mid-30s in Pittsburgh, the Seminoles (5-5, 3-4 ACC) and Panthers (6-4, 3-4 ACC) played a game befitting the chilly temperatures and venue. In the home of the Steelers, FSU's defense rose to the occasion with a stout performance against a Pitt offense led by third-string true freshman quarterback Corey Dailey. He finished the night with 157 yards on 16-for-34 passing, but his interception, a pass that deflected off the back of Deamonte Diggis and into the hands of Rylan Kennedy, proved costly. FSU's lone touchdown, a one-yard rush from Amari Thomas, came off the pick. FSU's Ashton Daniels protected the football and had minimal impact on the ground (nine rushes for 27 yards) against Pitt's elite run defense. Daniels finished the night 16-of-124 for 163 yards, with the Seminoles finding primary success on screen plays. He had a fumble, which came in the red zone, but it didn't lead to any Pitt points. Here are three takeaways from the Seminoles' victory over Pitt. Seminoles offense struggles to warm up on a cold night in Pittsburgh With the exception of wide receiver Jasen Lopez, the Seminoles got little production from the offense in the first half. Lopez recorded 72 total yards on five receptions, including 58 yards in the first half on three receptions, 46 of which came on a big third-down completion. Despite Lopez setting FSU up at the 10-yard line on that 46-yard reception, it only resulted in a field goal. The Seminoles consistently struggled to find the end zone, which led to multiple field goals. Gabe Panikowski, a week after scoring a touchdown, nailed three field goals: 27 yards, 37 yards, and a 47-yarder. FSU's run game struggled in the first half against the Panthers' top-ranked rush defense, holding the team to a total of 99 yards, including 25 yards in the first half. That number was the least since FSU's clash with Clemson in 2024. The Seminoles rushed for 74 yards in the second half, including a one-yard touchdown run from Amari Thomas, the only touchdown of the game for the program. In the fourth, FSU got advantageous field position after a turnover on downs, but a red zone fumble ruined a potential momentum-swinging drive. Daniels rushed for what would have been first-down yardage on third-and-six, but after he was engulfed in a mass of both Seminoles and Panthers, he fumbled. The play wasn't blown dead for forward progress, and the ball popped out of a mass of humanity and into the grateful hands of Pitt's Shawn Lee

technology.title: Millions of Americans are not taking their GLP-1 drugs as prescribed
technology.description: GLP-1 medications are everywhere these days. The peptide-based drugs are both highly effective and wildly popular for diabetes, weight loss and a growing range of connected chronic health conditions, including cardiovascular disease and obstructive sleep apnea. But, amid the boom, the latest data suggests millions of Americans have turned to unapproved versions and are using the potent drugs in ways doctors never intended, raising questions about what that real-world use means for safety and efficacy. In a study published this week , researchers at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention broke down survey data of GLP-1 use collected between July and August of 2025. Based on responses from over 8,000 US adults, the researchers estimate that about one in 10 US adults (9.8 percent) used a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist, aka GLP-1 medication, in 2025. That's around 27 million adults. The study was published in the CDC's Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report. Among GLP-1 users, nearly half (44 percent) reported using their GLP-1 in a way that was different from how it was prescribed. Users skipped doses, delayed getting refills, and used smaller doses than prescribed, among other changes. More than half of the people modifying how they used the drug said the changes were because of cost or availability reasons. Cost and access barriers were most pronounced among younger GLP-1 users. LogicLens aims to separate fact from fiction using the very same technology behind some of that slop: AI. LogicLens and Receipts claim to identify logical fallacies , flag reports that misrepresent information, detect content that attempts to polarize an issue, and the like. It also cites sources, so if, for example, you need to call someone out on their BS, you’ll have ammunition. Or, if you’re trying to fact-check something before sharing it, you can get a more accurate view of the situation, and maybe post something else instead. Using the Chrome extension is as simple as clicking on its icon in the list of extensions in the browser. On iOS, the Receipts app is found as a share option. Once it starts, LogicLens scans an article, post, video, etc. to find potential issues of factual or logical inconsistency and flags them for review. If the facts of the matter turn out to contradict your worldview, LogicLens’ creators say they’re not trying to be partisan - you may just not be as informed as you need to be, which hopefully their tool will assist with. “We're not trying to be the referee of truth,” the company’s about page states. “Instead, LogicLens helps uncover the context, so you can decide for yourself without the spin." Of course, AI is increasingly used for online analysis and content review, and LogicLens is no exception. technology.title: In elephants, the resilience of communities has its limits
technology.description: Elephants live in some of the most complex and resilient societies in the animal kingdom. Individuals die or move away, calves grow up, and newcomers join, but the local communities as a whole usually hold together. Long-term studies of African savanna elephants have shown that, even after poaching or other spikes in deaths, survivors tend to rebuild their lost connections over time. But a new study suggests that resilience may not keep the community intact when steady losses accumulate over time. Anastasia Madsen, a behavioral ecologist at the University of California, San Diego, and her colleagues analyzed 12 years of observations of wild Asian elephants in Sri Lanka. They found that, once losses began to outpace newcomers, the elephants’ society didn’t just get smaller. It fractured. Accidental savanna Udawalawe National Park in southern Sri Lanka was created in the 1970s around a reservoir on one of the country's four major rivers. “Before that, it was basically a tropical deciduous forest,” said Shermin de Silva, an ecologist at UC San Diego and senior author of the study (de Silva started the Udawalawe Elephant Research Project in 2006). science.title: SpaceX launches Starship on ambitious 22-hour Flight 15 test, but aborts booster 'chopsticks' catch (video)
science.description: null STARBASE, Texas — SpaceX launched the 15th test flight of its massive Starship rocket today (Nov. 13) and is preparing the vehicle's upper stage for its first-ever return to the launch site in less than 24 hours. Flight 15 lifted off from SpaceX 's Starbase facility here in South Texas at 5:47 p.m. ET (2247 GMT; 4:47 p.m. local Texas time). The towering Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage cleared the tower without incident and climbed into the skies under more than 18 million pounds of thrust from the booster's 33 Raptor 3 engines. The flight continued nominally through its initial ascent, with the successful execution of Super Heavy's main engine cutoff and Ship's subsequent hot-staging — firing its own Raptors during separation from the booster — about 2.5 minutes after launch. Following stage separation, Super Heavy reoriented for a planned return to Starbase as Ship powered its way toward low Earth orbit (LEO). SpaceX originally planned to catch Super Heavy with the Starbase launch tower's giant mechanical "chopstick" arms. But it wasn't to be: The company called off the catch attempt and brought the booster down for a controlled splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico about 6.5 minutes after launch, for reasons that were not immediately clear. A successful catch would have been a significant milestone for SpaceX and its efforts to design Starship as a fully and rapidly reusable launch vehicle. It would have been the first successful recovery of a Version 3 (V3) Super Heavy , which SpaceX began flying earlier this year. The company previously recovered three of its V1 Super Heavy vehicles and reused two of those in later flights. SpaceX's Starship megarocket launches on its 15th test flight from Starbase, Texas on Nov. 13, 2026. (Image credit: Future/Josh Dinner, Space.com) Ship goes to orbit Ship's Raptors continued to fire following stage separation, completing their first burn just after eight minutes into flight. All went according to plan after that for Ship as well: A second engine burn lasting about 20 seconds parked Ship in LEO at an altitude of around 170 miles (275 kilometers) at T+26 minutes and 10 seconds. "We’ve got a nominal orbit insertion, so Starship now in orbit around Earth for the second time ever," SpaceX's Dan Huot said during today's Flight 15 launch webcast. "That’s a really great moment." Ship first reached orbit on Flight 14 , which launched on Sept. 28. Ship carried 26 of SpaceX's Starlink V3 spacecraft, which were deployed into LEO on schedule today over a 42-minute span starting 35 minutes after launch. The upgraded wireless internet satellites are the second V3 batch to reach orbit, after a set of 26 that were delivered on Flight 14 . V3s are significantly more powerful than SpaceX's V2 Starlinks, which currently number more than 11,000 in LEO. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 13, 1971: NASA's Mariner 9 becomes 1st spacecraft to orbit Mars, revealing close looks at the Martian surface
science.description: null On Nov. 13, 1971, Mariner 9 became the first spacecraft to orbit Mars. At the time, scientists didn't know much about the Red Planet. NASA had several Mars flybys before Mariner 9 . Those flybys showed that Mars had a cratered surface , so some scientists thought that Mars looked just like the moon. Then Mariner 9 blew blew their minds. When Mariner 9 got to Mars , it arrived in the middle of a dust storm. It saw some tall structures sticking through the clouds. When the dust settled, images from Mariner 9 revealed that these structures were the tops of huge volcanoes. One volcano, Olympus Mons , is the tallest in the solar system. Mariner 9 also spotted an enormous canyon called Valles Marineris . This canyon is five times longer than the Grand Canyon in Arizona. Mariner 9 worked for one year in orbit. When it ran out of gas, NASA shut it off. But the spacecraft remains one of the most famous Mars voyagers of all time. The Mariner 9 spacecraft, seen here in a NASA model, was the first to orbit Mars in 1971. (Image credit: NASA) Here's why it mattered Mariner 9 cemented its place in space history when it entered into orbit around Mars, the first human-built spacecraft ever to do so. The NASA spacecraft actually beat the Soviet Union's own Mars 2 spacecraft to the Red Planet, even though Mars 2 "had an 11-day head start," NASA said in a mission description . (Mars 2 would go on to be the first human-built craft to impact the surface of Mars when it crashed into the Red Planet.) But it was the science from Mariner 9 that transformed Mars from a mysterious Red Planet into a full world for humans to explore. The Boldest Mars Missions in History The Mariner 9 mission first saw the peak of Olympus Mons on Mars in the midst of a global dust storm in 1971. (Image credit: NASA/JPL) Mariner 9 carried four primary instruments to study Mars, including a camera system for imaging, an ultraviolet spectrometer, an infrared spectrometer and an infrared radiometer. The probe mapped 85% of Mars with those tools during its nearly one-year mission. The Mariner 9 spacecraft discovered 20 giant volcanoes on Mars (including Olympus Mars) and made key observations to map Valles Marineris, which runs 2,500 miles (4,000 kilometers) long acros the Tharsis region and is 120 miles (200 km) wide. "The canyon was named in honor of Mariner 9," NASA said in an overview . In all, Mariner 9 took 7,329 photos of the surface of Mars, mapping the planet down to a resolution of between 1/2-1 mile (1-2 km). It also snapped at least 80 photos of Phobos and Deimos, the two small moons of Mars. By February 1972, Mariner 9's supply of gaseous nitrogen, which it used to feed its attitide control thrusters, had run dry. NASA finally shut down the mission in October 1972.
